subject: Materials Science
title: The Bessemer Process Revolution
description: A fast breakdown of The Bessemer Process Revolution for builders.

hook.text: Before 1856, making steel took days and cost a fortune. One inventor changed that.

buildup.text: Henry Bessemer blasted air through molten iron — the carbon burned away in minutes.

discovery.text: His converter turned expensive iron into cheap steel, slashing costs by 80 percent.

twist.text: Cheap steel made skyscrapers, railroads, and bridges suddenly affordable to build.

climax.text: The Bessemer process launched the Second Industrial Revolution almost single-handedly.

punchline.text: One blast of air built the modern world.

quiz.question: What did the Bessemer process do?
options: Removed carbon from iron using air to make cheap steel
Created stainless steel for the first time
